Mostly, yes — with one tug on the metaphor.

Clean separation is the right call. A modernization scorecard that blends adapter patches into "platform capability" is lying to itself, and anyone reading it later will discount the whole number once they figure that out. So forty points of new capability, stated as forty, is correct.

Where I'd push back is on treating the twenty as invisible. Ballast isn't nothing — leave it off the manifest and the ship looks faster on paper right up until it capsizes. Legacy maintenance is exactly the number that explains *why* modernization pace is what it is. Drop it and someone will eventually ask "you had sixty points of capacity, where'd a third of it go?" and you'll be reconstructing the answer under pressure.

So: two lines, not one, not zero.

- **Platform capability delivered: 40 pts**
- **Legacy sustainment (non-modernization): 20 pts**

Same scorecard, different buckets, no blending. The forty stays pure, and the twenty becomes an argument for retiring the adapters rather than a smudge on your progress. Over a few sprints, that second line trending down is one of the better modernization signals you can show.

If the scorecard format genuinely only has room for one number, then yes — forty, with a footnote. But I'd fight for the second line.

Nothing, to the engineering truth of it. Quite a lot, to how you label it.

The amendment changes what the client agreed to *pay for* and *call* the work. It doesn't change what the work *is*. Adapter hardening didn't become a new platform capability because a signature landed at 8am — the same commits are sitting in the same repo doing the same job they did yesterday. Paper reclassifies; it doesn't refactor.

So the scorecard gains a column, it doesn't lose a line:

- **Platform capability delivered: 40 pts** — new modernization surface
- **Adapter hardening: 20 pts** — legacy sustainment, contractually scoped as Phase 2 platform deliverable per amendment (date)
- **Milestone-eligible total: 60 pts**

That gets you everything you actually need. The bonus math is clean and defensible because it cites the executed amendment directly. The forty stays pure. And the twenty is still visible as what it is, so the modernization trendline doesn't get a fake bump that someone has to explain away in six months when adapter load hasn't dropped.

Notice the argument you made yesterday is the one to protect here. If ballast can become sail by amendment, then the scorecard measures paperwork, not progress — and you lose the ability to say "look, sustainment is trending down" because it'll just get re-scoped again whenever it's convenient. Keeping the categories honest is what keeps the forty worth anything.

Two flags. First, whoever reads this should never be surprised — bonus eligibility and modernization classification are different questions, and putting both on the page prevents anyone from later claiming they were shown one and understood the other. Second, "leadership re-scoped it *as* phase 2 capability" is doing a lot of work in that sentence. If the amendment text says the hardening is *part of* the Phase 2 platform scope, that's ordinary and fine. If it literally recharacterizes the nature of the work, read it again before you lean on it — that's the kind of wording that ages badly in an audit.

Bill the sixty. Report the forty. Footnote the twenty. Same answer as yesterday, now with a citation.

You're quoting me correctly, and the stance hasn't moved. The memo will show exactly forty in the modernization achievement metric, and the adapter work will not appear there.

But a milestone sign-off memo has a second job: it's the document that certifies contractual completion, and the contract as amended defines this milestone at sixty. If the memo only says forty and finance pays on sixty, the executive who signed it has certified something that doesn't match the invoice. That's not clean separation, that's a gap someone falls into later. So the twenty appears in the memo — in the milestone completion section, cited to the amendment, and nowhere near the modernization line.

Two metrics, two questions, one page. Placeholders in brackets.

**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** [Executive Sponsor]
**From:** [Name, Title]
**Date:** [Date]
**Re:** Milestone [N] Completion and Sign-Off — Sprint [ID]

**1. Purpose**

This memo requests executive sign-off on Milestone [N], completed at sprint close on [date], and documents the delivered scope against both the contractual milestone definition and the program modernization scorecard.

**2. Modernization Achievement Metric**

**Platform capability delivered: 40 points.**

This figure represents new platform capability only. It comprises [brief list of the capability epics/features]. It excludes all legacy sustainment and adapter work by design, so that the modernization trendline reflects forward progress on the target architecture and remains comparable across sprints.

**3. Contractual Milestone Completion**

Milestone [N] is complete at **60 points**, consisting of:

- Platform capability deliverables — 40 points (Section 2)
- Adapter hardening deliverables — 20 points, scoped to Phase 2 platform deliverables under Contract Amendment [number], executed [date]

All 60 points meet acceptance criteria as defined in the amended Statement of Work. Milestone completion bonus eligibility is established on this basis.

**4. Classification Note**

Adapter hardening is contractually part of the Phase 2 platform scope and is counted toward milestone completion accordingly. It is not counted in the modernization achievement metric, which measures new capability rather than sustainment of existing integrations. The two figures answer different questions and are not intended to reconcile to one another.

**5. Requested Action**

Sign-off confirming Milestone [N] completion at 60 points per Amendment [number], with modernization achievement recorded at 40 points.

_________________________
[Executive Sponsor], [Date]
